title: Accelerando
pitch: A family saga across three generations that runs straight through the technological singularity, from dot com hustlers to minds spread across the solar system.

chapters.g: Manfred Macx, a freelance idea giver, is contacted by uploaded lobster minds that want to escape.
Manfred's life frays as the economy speeds up and his family fights over his future.
Manfred loses his memory gear and with it much of himself.
Manfred's daughter Amber escapes her mother's control and heads for the outer solar system.
Amber's crew, travelling as uploaded minds, reaches an alien router and meets strange post singularity beings.
The travellers are trapped by alien entities inside virtual spaces.
Amber's son Sirhan and a family reunion in a solar system being rebuilt by machine minds.
Politics among humans who are now a minority in their own solar system.
What is left of humanity decides where to go next.

ideas: A singularity can feel gradual to those inside it.
Economic and legal systems may go strange as minds speed up.
Humans may become a minority among intelligences.
Uploading and copying change what identity means.

args.a: The novel shows how a takeoff could feel from the inside.
args.c: It is dense and playful, and its post human world is one imagined path among many.

args.a: Fast machine economies could push humans aside without hatred.
args.c: This idea, now often called gradual disempowerment, is debated in real research.

questions: When did the singularity happen in the story?
What would rights for corporations run by AI look like?
